_comment: Catalogue of the panel's Studies (courses): each detailed lecture lives in <id>.json (extracted from the slides). The exercises are console commands (/api/run). Study 3 points to the existing AI Lab pages.

bancadas.any: runs on a file, no RAN needed

estudos.resumo: The first Open RAN course of the specialization: the 5G that already exists (core, RAN, interfaces N1 to N11), the telco cloud and the motivation for opening up the RAN. In our lab this is Project 1: a complete Open5GS core with a simulated gNB and UE, where every interface can be seen working.
estudos.nota: Only lecture 01 was shared as a PDF; the others were presented in class.

estudos.resumo: The intelligent controller of the RAN: near-RT and non-RT RIC, the E2 and A1 interfaces, xApps and rApps, the SMO, and how all of this gets tested. In the lab it is Project 2: an OAI gNB with an E2 agent talking to FlexRIC, KPM and control xApps, and a Non-RT RIC that pushes policies down over A1.

estudos.titulo: AI and ML Applications in the RIC
estudos.resumo: Machine learning techniques applied to the RIC: regression, classification, clustering, anomaly detection, PCA, and the three cases from the reference paper (UE-TP, Localization, Predictive maintenance) with real data from the SUTD walk test. The panel's AI Lab is the material for this course: each lecture has theory, the experiment running live and a report.

externas.one: What AI/ML is, supervised and unsupervised, and the O-RAN loop.
Predict a number: the throughput of each UE (UE-TP).
Predict a category: the cell state.
Predict the UE's floor using only radio KPMs.
Detect the lost RRU from the UE side.
Find the cell that is out of pattern.
Summarize many KPIs into a few.
Apply a technique to a use case and deliver the report.

estudos.resumo: Where a network's data comes from (SMO, O1, E2, A1; PM, FM, KPM), how to store it (lake, warehouse, the raw/bronze/silver/gold zones), how to explore it (EDA, ETL, statistics, visualization) and how to turn it into indicators (KPIs/KQIs) and decisions. The capstone project (50% of the grade) uses the KPM telemetry from our lab: every group starts from the same data and each one answers a different question.

proximas.t: KPIs/KQIs and Checkpoint 1 (2 finalized indicators + visualizations)
Capacity and optimization; final technical checkpoint (recommendation/A1 + limitations)

dados.fonte: kpm-ue-tp-sample (the professor's offline track): 100 KPM measurements in 3 phases, baseline (20), stress (60) and recovery (20).
dados.troca: In the console, click the '💾 KPM (3 phases)' node in the execution strip to switch the source: the professor's sample, a file (.jsonl or .csv) or hand-pasted data. Only the professor switches it; everyone sees it.

temas.pergunta: Does the UE throughput rise and fall together with PRB usage and with delay?

ind.formula: mean(thp_ul) and p95(thp_ul), GROUP BY phase

temas.extra: Relationship: Pearson r = cov(x, y) / (sx * sy), global and within each phase (the global one mixes idle with load).
temas.rec: If throughput drops while PRB is high (poorly served user), propose prioritization in an A1 policy (dry-run).

temas.pergunta: At which moments does the network leave its normal state in a sustained way, rather than in an isolated spike?

ind.formula: score = |x - median_baseline| / max(MAD, 1); anomalous if score > 3.5 in at least 2 of the 3 metrics

ind.nome: Intensity of the deviation under load
ind.formula: mean and maximum of the sample's highest score, in the stress phase

temas.extra: MAD = median(|x - median(x)|) computed on the baseline only. It is the same algorithm as the professor's model.json (robust-baseline-mad); the 'apply' decision comes out when the whole window (5 samples) is anomalous.
temas.rec: With most of the window anomalous, a decision to reduce UL congestion over A1 (dry-run). Isolated spikes become false alarms, not decisions.

temas.pergunta: When does the radio delay suggest that the user experience may be poor?

ind.formula: median(delay_dl) and p95(delay_dl), GROUP BY phase

ind.nome: Fraction of time in high delay

temas.extra: Cross-check: high delay WITH low throughput reinforces the poor-experience hypothesis; high delay with high throughput is a load queue. The 100 ms threshold is justified and adjustable.
temas.rec: Sustained delay above the threshold under load: investigate the session and prioritize sensitive traffic (A1 dry-run). Delay is a proxy: there is no MOS score.

temas.pergunta: Do the data show saturation that justifies a capacity alert?

ind.formula: mean(prb_ul) and p95(prb_ul), GROUP BY phase
n( MM5(prb_ul) > 0.8 * PRB_max  AND  MM5(thp_ul) < 0.5 * p95(thp_ul) ) / n

temas.extra: MM5 = 5-sample moving average: it looks at the trend, not at a single instant. A full radio with high throughput is capacity in use, not at risk.
temas.rec: Only with saturated PRB AND falling throughput: capacity alert and load-relief intent over A1 (dry-run).

temas.pergunta: How do we summarize the experiment into cell indicators, and what is the limit of that in the lab?

ind.formula: mean(thp_ul) per phase; sum = mean * n_UE when there are several UEs

temas.extra: It is the GROUP BY of the mini-lake's gold zone. With 1 UE, mean = sum: the aggregation is didactic, not campus statistics.
temas.rec: Compare the normal phase with the load phase and state the limit: few UEs in RFSIM.

temas.pergunta: In which stretches is the load low enough to think about saving energy, without switching anything off?

ind.nome: Fraction of time in low load
ind.formula: low load = prb_ul <= 0.1 * PRB_max  AND  thp_ul <= 0.1 * p95(thp_ul); n(low) / n

ind.nome: Throughput and delay in those windows
ind.formula: mean(thp_ul) and median(delay_dl) only over the low-load samples

temas.extra: Before any intent, check that the delay stays acceptable (<= 100 ms) in the low-load windows.
temas.rec: Energy-saving intent over A1 (dry-run) only: the lab does not control RU power and nothing is switched off.

temas.pergunta: Faced with degradation, which decision rule would be safe for proposing a QoS policy?

ind.formula: degradation = delay_dl > 100 ms  OR  (prb_ul > 0.8 * PRB_max  AND  thp_ul < 0.5 * p95); n(rule) / n
rising edges of the rule (false to true); 'sustained' = 3 consecutive samples

temas.extra: The persistence filter avoids reacting to an isolated spike (false alarms in the baseline and in the recovery). The ASCII timeline shows where the rule fires.
temas.rec: Candidate A1 policy (UE/QoS scope, priority, steering) with human validation before automating. We do not claim that handover or path changed.
